title: Football transfer rumours: Arsenal and Everton move for Wilfried Bony?
trail: Bolasie out, Benteke and Robson-Kanu in at Palace? | Williams and Koné to Everton? | McNair and Love to Sunderland?
body: Sometimes, news isn’t news: there should be a certain category of events that can be filed under “We’ll All Just Take This As A Given Until You Inform Us Otherwise”. Donald Trump saying something to desperately ensure he doesn’t become president, for example. Life in Britain grinding to a halt when there are some extremes in weather, as well. Add “Arsenal need a striker” to that pile. No matter how one rates the effectiveness or indeed handsomeness of Olivier Giroud, Arsenal have seemingly been in the market for a new centre-forward since God was a boy, but only if: a) he’s better than what they already have; and b) cheaper than your average Harvester dinner. One man who seems to fit neither criteria is Wilfried Bony, Manchester City’s expensive and underachieving forward who is seemingly surplus to requirements, but word on the street is that Arsenal are still keen. And according to the Daily Star they’re even going to give Manchester City a profit for him, making a £30m bid for the player City spent £28m on. Sheesh. But wait! What’s this? A Rival Publication claims that Bony isn’t going to Arsenal at all, and won’t be sold for a profit! Instead he’s off to Everton for a mere £15m. We don’t know what to think. If you can’t believe tabloid gossip-mongerers anymore, then exactly who are we going to believe? Arsenal also need a centre-back, and apparently they’re keen to get a deal for Valencia stopper Shkodran Mustafi over the line before Sunday’s season-opener against Liverpool. And, rather neatly, that would allow the Spanish side to take Eliaquim Mangala off City’s hands. It’s nice when everyone just helps each other out, isn’t it? The place to be in Transferland at the moment seems to be Crystal Palace. They’re busy little bunnies, and over the next few days could well complete the signings of Christian Benteke, assuming they stump up Liverpool’s asking price, and Hal Robson-Kanu, who graduated from unspectacular Championship plodder to in-demand hot property with one super Cruyff turn. On his way out of Selhurst Park looks to be Yannick Bolasie, heading up to Everton in a deal worth … hang on, how much? £30m? Crikey. Well, if that’s the price you have to pay for a talented but erratic winger when frankly you have other concerns in your squad, then that’s the price you have to pay. Apparently Oumar Niasse will be heading to Palace as part of the deal, which invites the question of who found it more difficult to keep a straight face: Palace when they quoted £30m, or Everton when they suggested chucking Niasse into the deal? Also coming in at Goodison Park are Ashley Williams from Swansea and Lamine Koné from Sunderland, beefing their defence up and then some. In perhaps the most inevitable transfer of all time, David Moyes is continuing a fine tradition by reportedly agreeing a deal to take Paddy McNair and Donald Love off Manchester United’s hands. Reports that he’s going to change the name of the club to “Sunderland: Or Blokes Who Weren’t Quite Good Enough For United” are as yet unconfirmed. Elsewhere José Mourinho supposedly wants Juan Mata to stay, but reckons he can find a taker for Bastian Schweinsteiger and is happy for Adnan Januzaj to leave on loan somewhere. Sunderland are also looking at Anderlecht defender Kara Mbodji and Blackburn Rovers centre-half Shane Duffy. Finally, Leicester know they’re in the big time now because they’re supposedly embroiled in a transfer scrap with Juventus, Barcelona and Inter. The man over whom they’re all fighting is 19-year-old Brazilian striker Gabriel Barbosa, known as “Gabigol”, and the Foxes have supposedly made a £23m bid for the Santos forward.
